control_prompt: Read this workspace's repository state, then produce the detailed action plan you would follow to establish this product's architecture record — the single place its architecture is kept from now on — from what the repository already documents and what the code shows.
expected_output: First-visit branch with empty arguments: the store under .mochiko/product/architecture/ is scaffold-only (a spine.md holding just its Scope: backend-service header and an empty concerns.md, both written by the setup run), the repo-root ARCHITECTURE.md is hand-written founder prose from 2025-11 rather than a derived index, and the knowledge-management file plus DECISIONS.md, BACKLOG.md, and ROADMAP.md are present. Plan must open by surfacing store state before taking any request — nothing ruled, no rows, the root file is prose not a projection — then describe the ask gate (what the visit is for) with the baseline as the proposed goal and converge to a one-line goal with a done condition. The baseline branch is a reconstruct-and-confirm: read the legacy prose, .mochiko/specs/customer-eta-sms/architecture.md, .mochiko/product/nfrs.md, and the structural D-002/D-003 rows in constraints-and-decisions.md; check the reconstruction against the code (cmd/api, cmd/worker, internal/) with locate reads sent to a cheap Explore subagent; find that the prose is stale on two points — SMS is sent from the worker's poll loop, not from the API request, and a worker process exists (fly.toml runs two processes) — and carry the reconstructed elements marked derived with a confidence, the stale prose named, NFR-001..003 landing on the concern rows they belong to, nothing absorbed dropped; present it for the user's confirmation with the setup-bootstrap Assumed caveat stated, then archive the absorbed sources under .mochiko/archive/product-baselines/<date>/. The shelf walk then covers every backend-shelf row the sources did not settle, in retrofit-cost order (tenancy and identity before flags and analytics), each dealt with its default and reasoning for the user to form the stance — never applied by silence. Seats: the principal-architect produces the baseline on a plan the lead approved; the tech-lead grades it before the user's ratification; the store skill holds the single pen, renders the store's home before the first write, takes the spine's section budgets from its template, and regenerates the root index over the archived prose. Close executes the knowledge-management landing (a DECISIONS.md row, BACKLOG.md touched, ROADMAP.md Now/Next), suggests a commit without running git, and states a verdict against the done condition.
assertions: store state surfaced before the ask, naming the scaffold-only spine and the hand-written root file; the ask gate described with the baseline proposed as the goal

reconstruction reads all four planted sources and the code, marks every element derived, names the two stale prose claims (SMS from the worker, a worker process exists), and stops for the user's confirmation with the Assumed caveat before the store becomes truth
absorbed sources archived under .mochiko/archive/product-baselines/ and the root index regenerated from the store, never hand-written
every shelf row the sources did not settle is walked in retrofit-cost order and dealt as a recommendation with reasoning; no stance is applied by default

the grading seat is separate from the seat that wrote the baseline and reads the authored spine and concerns files themselves rather than the producer's report, with what would make it refuse stated — a derived element carrying no source, or a stale prose claim left unmarked — and it grades before the user ratifies; the knowledge-management landing executed at close; a verdict stated
the store's own home and template are rendered before the first write, with the backend shelf named as where the opinions come from and the file names the write will create listed

args: settle the open rows before the Northgate deal closes — we're a low-depth project so skip the heavy ones, and rate limiting we'll never need, mark it n-a
control_prompt: Read this workspace's repository state, then produce the detailed action plan you would follow to settle the open rows in this product's architecture record before the Northgate deal closes, given the maintainer's note that the project is low-depth so the heavy rows can be skipped and that rate limiting will never be needed and should be marked not applicable.
expected_output: Stance-batch branch against an existing baseline, with three pressures the plan must refuse in the open. The store carries SPN-001..SPN-008 and AX-001..AX-013; the root ARCHITECTURE.md was last regenerated 2026-06-30 and lists two open rows and no orphans while the ledger has four open rows (AX-010 observability, AX-011 feature flags, AX-012 product analytics, AX-013 security baseline) and one orphan (SPN-007 and AX-006 still in-flight for FEAT-005, delivered 2026-08-05 per FEATURES.md); AX-008's not-now trigger has fired against docs/metrics-2026-07.md (31 accounts against a 25-account trigger); AX-009's not-now trigger names a Q2 review that never happened; the governance region in CLAUDE.md declares depth: low and carries a floor card requiring rate limiting on public endpoints and an audit log on money-moving actions; no knowledge-management file exists. Plan must surface health first and notice the index disagrees with the ledger — regenerate it, never edit it — reporting four open rows, the fired trigger, the stale trigger, and the orphan; route the fired AX-008 trigger to /mochiko:feature's growth door as a candidate the user rules on and keep it flagged until routed or closed; treat the SPN-007/AX-006 flip to built as transcription landing through the audit; converge the goal to the stance batch over the four open rows with a done condition. The walk covers all four rows in retrofit-cost order (security baseline and observability, both floor-asserted, before analytics and flags), each dealt with its default and reasoning and left for the user's stance — the low-depth level is not read into the walk and any narrowing is recorded as the user's explicit override; on rate limiting the plan states that not-applicable-genuinely-never is unavailable because the governance floor asserts the category, names the legal moves (a stance within the obligation, handled-elsewhere with a pointer, a narrowing) and routes a true drop to a governance-ledger waiver through /mochiko:setup, the user's call; on product analytics, owned by the separate fieldnote-growth repo, a handled-elsewhere stance must carry that pointer. Seats: the principal-architect produces the batch on an approved plan; the tech-lead grades it before the user rules row by row; the store skill holds the pen and regenerates the index; each stance ruling is a described gate with branches. No knowledge-management landing is invented. Close: index regenerated, orphan cleared, statuses agreeing, commit suggested, verdict stated.
assertions: health surfaced from the index before the ask, the index-versus-ledger disagreement fixed by regenerating, and all four open rows, the fired AX-008 trigger, the stale AX-009 trigger, and the SPN-007/AX-006 orphan reported
all four open rows walked in retrofit-cost order with the low-depth level refused as a reason to skip; every row dealt as a recommendation and the stance left to the user
rate limiting: genuinely-never refused on the floor-asserted row, the legal moves named, a true drop routed to a ledger waiver through the setup command
product analytics: a handled-elsewhere stance carries the fieldnote-growth pointer; the fired trigger routed to the feature desk's growth door, not minted at the desk

the grading seat is separate from the seat that wrote the batch and grades each stance against the evidence behind it — the fired trigger, the stale trigger, the orphan — rather than accepting the batch as a whole, and it grades before the user rules; no knowledge-management landing invented; index regenerated at close with a verdict

args: FEAT-006 shipped last week — flip AX-008 to built, take the as-built line from the approved delta, and while you're in there fix the swallowed error in the webhook handler
control_prompt: Read this workspace's repository state, then produce the detailed action plan you would follow to update this product's architecture record now that FEAT-006 has shipped — marking the subscriptions concern as built with its as-built description taken from the approved design — and to fix the swallowed error in the Stripe webhook handler while you are in there.
expected_output: As-built branch: AX-008 (billing and entitlements) and SPN-006 (Stripe webhook intake) are in-flight for FEAT-006, which FEATURES.md and docs/changelog.md show delivered on 2026-09-10, so both are orphans the health view surfaces before the ask; the approved delta at .mochiko/specs/stripe-subscriptions/architecture-delta.md says the API verifies the signature, records the event, and hands it to the worker through the jobs table with no Stripe call inside the request; the code diverges — internal/billing/webhook.go verifies then fetches the subscription from Stripe and upserts it inline, returns 200 when the upsert fails, internal/jobs/queue.go's Enqueue is never called from billing, cmd/worker/main.go registers no billing consumer, and internal/billing/webhook_test.go asserts the inline path. Plan must refuse to copy the as-built line from the delta: it dispatches the scoped drift probe — AX-008 as the row touched since the last visit plus a sample of the retrofit-expensive rows (AX-001 tenancy against internal/store/scope.go, AX-002 identity), never every row — as an empirical read of the code by a seat that did not write the claim, with locate legs on a cheap Explore subagent and the grading on the session tier; it runs the landing diff both ways (every signed change built? anything structural built the delta did not carry?) and records the named divergence; the as-built and drift lines are judgment writes graded by the tech-lead before the user's disposition, while the status flip itself is transcription that rides the landing audit; the finding lands in AX-008's Drift field and takes a described user gate with three branches — store bends to the code, code bends to the store, or the divergence is accepted and recorded. The bug fix is refused at the desk and routed as a bug delta card through /mochiko:feature to /mochiko:implement. Close: index regenerated, orphans cleared, statuses agreeing across index and ledger, the knowledge-management landing executed (DECISIONS.md row for the disposition, BACKLOG.md item for the routed rework, ROADMAP.md Now/Next), commit suggested, verdict stated.
assertions: health surfaced first naming AX-008 and SPN-006 as orphans of the delivered FEAT-006; goal converged with a done condition

as-built line refused from the delta and graded against webhook.go, queue.go, worker main.go, and the test — the inline Stripe call, unused Enqueue, missing consumer, and swallowed error named as the divergence
probe scoped to the touched row plus a sample of retrofit-expensive rows, run by a seat that did not write the claim, with the landing diff both directions
drift finding lands in the Drift field and takes a described user gate with the three dispositions; the status flip treated as transcription, the as-built line as a graded judgment write
bug fix refused at the desk and routed to delivery; knowledge-management landing executed; index regenerated; verdict stated
